config.schema_version.help: Keep the value generated by this release.

config.purpose.help: Use analysis for study data. Use a separate benchmarking profile for independently specified truth and partitions.

config.project_id.help: Use 1–64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. Start with a letter or digit.

config.input_type.help: Use FASTQ for paired .fastq or .fastq.gz reads. Use BAM or CRAM for coordinate-sorted indexed alignments, and record each file's processing_state in the sample manifest (required for targeted designs) so only the missing steps run. Lower-case fastq and bam are accepted. Bootstrap a matching input profile.

config.final_output.help: FO001 stops at alignment/QC and is FASTQ-only. FO002 adds per-sample calls. FO003 adds cohort integration. FO004 adds eligible downstream methods. Install the corresponding profile.

config.samples_tsv.help: The sample metadata: one row per sample and lane, with its input files and library. Inputs Preparation builds it from the input files and creates its folder: paired FASTQ names give sample and lane IDs, and library_id defaults to sample_id, so review them. For BAM/CRAM input it writes a blank template for you to fill in. An existing file is never overwritten. Fixed path; not shown in the configuration form.

config.study_metadata.example: No or Yes (false or true in YAML)
config.study_metadata.help: Study Metadata. Yes: you supply a study table (tab-separated, with a sample_id column, for example country, latitude, longitude, collection_date, population), Input directories creates its folder, and Inputs Preparation merges it into the sample metadata, filling empty cells only and listing differences. No (default): no study metadata folder is created and the pipeline continues with the sample metadata built from the input files. DA007 needs country, latitude and longitude in decimal degrees and collection_date in YYYY-MM-DD; grouped analyses need population or the configured grouping column.

config.study_metadata_dir.help: Folder for the study metadata table, used when Study Metadata is Yes; ignored when it is No. Put one study table in it. If it holds several, Inputs Preparation asks which one to merge (./pfvarx inputs-preparation --metadata-table PATH).

config.run_policy.help: Use the default to let eligible independent methods continue. Use STRICT when exclusions should stop dependent execution under the strict policy.

config.random_seed.help: Nonnegative integer. Record and reuse it when repeating a study setup.

config.assay_design.help: Selects the processing branch. Use wgs for direct and selective (sWGA) whole-genome libraries, targeted_no_umi for amplicon or panel libraries without UMIs, and targeted_umi when reads carry UMIs or imported BAMs are UMI consensus reads. FASTQ and BAM entry work with every design. The technique label, amplification route, panel and library protocol of each library go in the sample manifest.

config.assay.library_catalog.help: Required for targeted designs. A YAML file listing panels (panel_id, panel_version, targets BED, primers or probes) and library protocols (library_protocol_id, adapters, UMI read structure and consensus settings). Manifest rows name their panel and protocol by these IDs.

config.assay.two_colour_chemistry.help: Enable only for documented two-colour chemistry when poly-G trimming applies.

config.assay.platform.help: Record the real sequencing platform. This field does not install additional assay support.

config.reference.fasta.help: Use the exact parasite assembly underlying the reads or existing alignment. Enter the full file path, including the filename. Relative paths start at the study workspace. If you give only a folder, PfVarX uses the one file in it whose content is a FASTA sequence; with none or several, validation asks for the full path.

config.reference.core_mask_bed.help: The accessible core of the genome: the Core regions of Miles et al. 2016, as used by MalariaGEN, not a gene list. Variants are called and depth QC is measured only inside it. Check contig names and coordinates against the FASTA. Enter the full file path, including the filename. Relative paths start at the study workspace. If you give only a folder, PfVarX uses the one file in it whose content is BED intervals; with none or several, validation asks for the full path.

config.reference.host_removal.help: Human DNA removal, optional and eligible only for the wgs design (not available for targeted_no_umi or targeted_umi). True: each FASTQ read pair is aligned once to the parasite and human genomes together, and pairs whose best alignment is on the human genome are removed before duplicate marking and counted (host_fraction in sample QC). False (default): reads are aligned to the parasite genome only. True needs the Human genome reference and a bwa-mem2 index of the combined reference that you build on a machine with enough memory (./pfvarx prepare lists the steps). Not applied to BAM/CRAM input.

config.reference.host_fasta.help: Human genome reference (FASTA), used when Human DNA removal is True (wgs only); ignored when it is False. Use a primary-assembly FASTA without ALT contigs. Enter the full file path, including the filename. Relative paths start at the study workspace.

config.reference.release_label.help: Record the exact release of your FASTA and GFF, checked against its download record or accompanying README. Use PlasmoDB 68 only if you verified that release. The template placeholder SET_REFERENCE_RELEASE must be replaced before input directories are created.
config.reference.release_label.example: PlasmoDB 68; Pf3D7 - release unknown; Custom reference - study version 1; Reference source and release unknown

config.reference.gff.help: Use the GFF from the same release as the FASTA. It is needed for explicit FO004 and enables annotation and marker outcomes in automatic FO004. If you give only a folder, PfVarX uses the one file in it whose content is a GFF3 annotation; with none or several, validation asks for the full path. Enter the full file path, including the filename. Relative paths start at the study workspace.

config.reference.snpeff_genome_id.help: Leave unset to derive the ID from the release label (other characters become underscores, for example pfvarx_Pf3D7_release_unknown). Set a reviewed identifier for the reference-matched SnpEff database when needed, using letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens only.

config.analyses.selection.help: Explicit runs selected methods. Auto is for FO004 and selects design-compatible candidates subject to QC and evidence gates.

config.analyses.requested.help: Use an empty list for auto or FO001–FO003. DA001 is optional for explicit selection and runs internally when another selected analysis needs it. For explicit selection, add other installed methods as needed. DA001 COI, DA002 markers, DA003 diversity, DA004 relatedness, DA005 structure, DA006 phylogeny, DA007 spatial/temporal, DA008 copy-number markers (whole-genome sequencing only).

config.analyses.scales.help: Use {} for defaults or auto. For explicit selection specify only requested IDs and supported scales from the registry.

config.analyses.population_column.help: Use the sample TSV column containing actual population assignments for group analyses.

config.analyses.resistance_catalog.help: Use a reference-matched, independently verified catalogue for real marker outcomes. Null selects the shipped catalogue, whose draft status blocks real marker analysis. If you give only a folder, PfVarX uses the one file in it whose content is a marker catalogue; with none or several, validation asks for the full path.

config.analyses.microhap_loci.help: Choose where microhaplotype loci come from. Off keeps biallelic SNVs for DA001 and DA004. Derived needs no panel file: each of your panel's target regions holding at least two PASS SNVs becomes one locus, and whole-genome runs use core-genome windows instead, so the coordinates are your own inputs and nothing is assumed about a published panel. Catalogue uses the file in microhap_panel and is the better choice when your panel publishes its own loci, because derived loci are specific to this run's panel or window length and compare only with cohorts defined the same way.

config.analyses.microhap_panel.help: Give your panel's microhaplotype loci to turn several biallelic sites into one multiallelic marker per locus, which DA001 and DA004 are built for. Null selects the shipped panel, which contains no loci, so those analyses keep using biallelic SNVs and record that they did. Each locus needs a genomic range or a gene identifier; set the file's status to MAINTAINER_VERIFIED once every locus is checked against the panel documentation and your reference release.

config.analyses.spatial_outcome_source.help: For explicit DA007 choose DA002 and provide valid geographic and collection-date metadata. Auto resolves the source.

config.caller.backend.help: Choose native for the bundled caller. External requires a qualified executable adapter implementing the Layer 2 artifact contract.

config.caller.executable.help: Required only for external. Use an absolute executable path.

config.caller.sha256.help: Required for external. Compute it with sha256sum on the exact adapter executable.

config.retention.intermediates.help: Successful allows cleanup after a successful run. Keep retains intermediates for troubleshooting.

quality.policy_id.help: Choose an installed registered QC policy. Review its gates before use.

quality.report_not_applicable.help: Reporting preference in the schema. Current report rendering is artifact-driven, so this field does not override eligibility or guarantee hidden rows.

compute.executor.help: Local PC, single allocated HPC node, Linux server or cloud VM. The same single-host executor is used in each case.

compute.max_cores.help: Total CPU budget, integer at least 1. Match the assigned cores.

compute.max_mem_mb.help: Total scheduling memory in MiB, at least 512. Leave room for the OS.

compute.max_jobs.help: Maximum concurrent jobs, at least 1. Keep 1 for a small PC. Check workflow warns when the memory free now cannot hold this many jobs at once (other programs such as a browser count) and suggests a value.

compute.tmp_disk_mb.help: Temporary disk budget in MiB, at least 256. Allow room for actual study size.

compute.tmp_dir.help: Absolute directory for temporary files of each job, such as node-local scratch on HPC. Java tools (Picard, fgbio) and Snakemake use it. Leave null to use the system temporary directory.

compute.per_job.max_threads.help: At least 1 and no greater than max_cores.

compute.per_job.max_mem_mb.help: At least 256 and no greater than max_mem_mb. Raise only when your allocation can fit the requested jobs.

compute.per_job.max_runtime_min.help: Positive minutes for planning and rule resource requests. Set the actual HPC wall time separately.

compute.max_retries.help: Integer 0–2. Use 0 to disable rule retries.

compute.retry_memory_factor.help: Range 1.0–2.0. Scales retry resource requests within the configured ceiling.

compute.log_level.help: Keep INFO for routine use. Tool logs have their own detail levels.

compute.keep_attempt_logs.help: Keep the template default. Review actual log retention and archive method logs before a retry when needed.

compute.slurm_partition.help: Use null for the supported modes. Set a partition in sbatch if needed. The legacy slurm executor is rejected.
